title: Measure your channels, check readiness, set your brand rules

say: Measure your channels, check you are ready, and set your brand rules.

say: Before you add anything new, measure what you have. Amaka sells her jars directly for about 4,000 naira. Last month she sold 400 jars.
260 jars went through WhatsApp and Instagram. That is 1,040,000 naira.
100 jars sold at her Saturday market stall, for 400,000 naira.
And one salon bought 40 jars at a trade price of 2,800 naira. That is 112,000 naira.
Her total is 1,552,000 naira. WhatsApp and Instagram bring 67.0% of it. So two thirds of her income depends on her phone and her social media accounts.
If that account is hacked, most of her month is gone. Take your figures from your sales book or bank statements, not from memory.
Most new shop deals fail because the supplier was not ready. Score yourself 0, 1 or 2 on five areas.

panel.heading: The five-part readiness check
items: Product consistency: every batch the same
Packaging and paperwork: label, CAC, NAFDAC where needed
Capacity: extra units without starving buyers
Pricing headroom: profit left after their margin
Cash and admin: fund stock, invoice, keep an order log

say: A pharmacy chain with 4 branches asks Amaka for 24 jars per branch every two weeks. That is 192 jars a month.

panel.heading: Can Amaka supply a pharmacy chain?
items: Chain asks: 4 branches x 24 jars x 2 = 192 jars
New total 592, but her maximum is 500
Cash tied up: 192 x 1,900 = 364,800 naira
Start with 2 branches: 96 jars, about 182,400 naira

say: Here is the rule. If a new channel takes stock your direct customers were waiting for, you swap a known, full-price buyer for an unproven, lower-price one. Protect them first, then add.

panel.rule: Never starve your loyal buyers. Protect existing demand first.

say: First, set a recommended retail price, so a customer sees roughly the same price everywhere.

panel.heading: Three price rules that protect you

cards.d: Advise one shelf price, the RRP, so a customer sees roughly the same price wherever she shops.
Your lowest trade price, from cost. Cost 1,900 naira, 25% margin: 1,900 / 0.75 = about 2,533.
Do not sell online far below the shop price. Shop at 4,000, you at 3,200: the shop stops reordering.

say: Second, set your floor price from your cost, not from a buyer's pressure. If a jar costs 1,900 naira and you need 25% margin, the floor is about 2,533 naira.

say: Third, keep price parity. If a pharmacy sells at 4,000 naira and you sell at 3,200 online, the pharmacy loses customers to you and soon stops reordering.

say: Outright purchase means the shop buys your stock and owns it. Unsold units are its problem, unless you agree otherwise.

panel.heading: Outright purchase or consignment
left: The shop buys and owns the stock
Unsold units are the shop's problem
You know what you will be paid
right: You still own stock on the shelf
Shop pays only for what sells
Easier to get in, riskier for you
Write who pays for damage or loss

say: Consignment means you still own the stock, and the shop pays only for what sells after each count.
It is easier to get in, but riskier for you, so write down who pays for damaged or missing units.

say: If a term is not written down, each side remembers it differently. Amaka's one-page agreement said damage must be reported within 48 hours.
When a jar arrived cracked, that rule settled it in one message instead of an argument.

panel.heading: Every agreement covers these six
items: Products, sizes and trade prices
Order minimum and delivery
Payment terms and method
Outright or consignment stock
Returns, damage and expiry
Review date and ending

say: To remember. Measure your channels from real records. Score your readiness, and check capacity and cash before you say yes. Set your prices from cost and keep parity. And put every agreement in writing, with your walk-away point decided before you negotiate.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Measure each channel's share before adding a new one
Score readiness before you pitch; 8 to 10 means go
Calculate capacity and the cash credit terms tie up
Set an RRP, a floor price from cost, and keep parity
Agree terms in writing and know your walk-away point
